summary: Lewis County lookout on Boistfort Peak: cabin from 1919, 82-83 ft tower from 1936, staffed into 1961, abandoned in 1967; register says now gone.

facts.design: 15-by-18-foot shake cabin (1919); 82-foot treated-timber tower with 7-by-7-foot cab (1936), shortened to 55 feet in 1960
facts.status_note: Abandoned entirely in 1967; the register says the lookout is now gone

events.note: Cabin dated 1919 by the register; the 1919 annual report says a lookout building was erected
1920 annual report says a lookout house was constructed that year; differs from the 1919 date
Weather station installed on the summit with Weather Bureau cooperation; instruments kept at the lookout
H.O. Roundtree named as lookout in charge (1925); also named 1931 and 1936
82-foot treated-timber tower with 7x7 cab (register); an annual report gives 83 feet
Page lists activation on March 4, 1942, with the Olympia Filter Center
Edgar Thomas manned the lookout in summer 1958
Shortened to 55 feet with a live-in DNR cab placed on top
Edgar Thomas named to man the lookout again in 1961
Abandoned entirely in 1967; the register says the lookout is now gone
Registered November 26, 2011 as US 1153, WA 61; nominated by Ray Kresek

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register dates the cabin to 1919 and the 1919 annual report describes a lookout building erected that year; the 1920 annual report says a lookout house was constructed in 1920. The sources differ on the year.
The register says the 1936 tower was 82 feet; a Division of Forestry annual report says 83 feet. The record's 25.3 m equals 83 feet, so it follows the annual report.
A 1937 survey station description calls the tower a Forest Service lookout; the register and the 1958-60 DNR report place the lookout with the state Division of Forestry/DNR.

notes_for_editor: The Forest Lookouts page transcribes newspaper items and annual reports, cited as it cites them; the originals were not checked. The page marks 'Removed' above a survey-marker entry without saying what was removed, so it is not used as a fate claim. The firelookout.com header ('R.I.P. 1919-1960?; 1960-?') has question marks and is not used. Access today is unknown; no access level recorded. Photo credits on firelookout.com (Fire Lookout Museum, Duane Klusman) have no URL, so no photo added.
